report.source_text: A 58-year-old man initially presented to his dentist with a chief complaint of tongue discomfort with unusual indentations (figure 1A,B). Due to his symptoms and findings he was referred to otolaryngology for further evaluation. Otolaryngology evaluation and examination was followed by treatment for oral thrush and tongue biting counselling, as it was determined that his indentations were likely due to unintentional biting. In addition to his tongue complaints, he reported a progressive dyspnoea with activity. The bilateral periorbital plaques (figure 1A,C) developed with the onset of his tongue discomfort. However, he did not seek medical attention for the periorbital plaques. His tongue symptoms remained stable for a year while the dyspnoea on exertion was not associated with paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea, orthopnoea or angina.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Systemic AL amyloidosis (lambda light chain type) secondary to high-risk plasma cell myeloma with cardiac infiltration
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old man presented with concurrent onset of tongue discomfort with indentations and bilateral periorbital plaques. Over the subsequent year, he developed progressive dyspnoea on exertion without orthopnoea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea, or angina, culminating in acute heart failure syndrome (NYHA class II) with physical examination findings of pitting lower extremity edema, jugular venous distention, abdominal distention, and mild bibasilar rales. History of bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome with surgical release 2 years prior to symptom onset suggested earlier amyloid deposition in peripheral nerves. Otolaryngology re-evaluation noted absence of overt macroglossia but tongue biopsy was performed due to persistent symptoms. Tongue biopsy histopathology demonstrated AL amyloid with positive Congo red stain and mass spectrometry confirmation. Immunofixation study revealed monoclonal free lambda light chain (markedly elevated at 2297 mg/dL). Bone marrow biopsy showed 95% plasma cell myeloma with concomitant amyloidosis and high-risk cytogenetics (t(4;14) translocation with IGH deletion in 90.5% of nuclei, monosomy 13q deletion in 93.5% of nuclei). Transthoracic echocardiogram revealed increased ventricular wall thickness with concentric hypertrophy, enlarged atria, small pericardial effusion, and mild diffuse thickening of mitral and tricuspid valves consistent with infiltrative cardiomyopathy. Cardiac biomarkers were elevated (serum troponin 0.050 ng/mL, proBNP 3407 pg/mL). Additional laboratory findings included microcytic anemia (hemoglobin 11.7 g/dL, MCV 78.0 fL), hypoalbuminemia (3.3 g/dL), and proteinuria (552 mg/dL). Treatment was initiated with bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone for myeloma, doxycycline for cardiac amyloidosis, and supportive heart failure management. One year after treatment initiation, the patient completed induction therapy, consolidation with autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, and was on bortezomib maintenance therapy with complete resolution of heart failure symptoms, discontinuation of diuretics, and return to normal functional status (bowling regularly, planning travel).

Echocardiography findings consistent with infiltrative cardiomyopathy: increased ventricular wall thickness with concentric hypertrophy, enlarged atria, small pericardial effusion, mild diffuse thickening of mitral and tricuspid valves
Monoclonal free lambda light chain identified on immunofixation study with markedly elevated free lambda at 2297 mg/dL
Bone marrow biopsy demonstrated 95% plasma cell myeloma with concomitant amyloidosis, t(4;14) translocation with IGH deletion (90.5% of nuclei), monosomy 13q deletion (93.5% of nuclei)
Cardiac biomarkers elevated: serum troponin 0.050 ng/mL (mildly elevated), proBNP 3407 pg/mL (elevated)
Laboratory findings: microcytic anemia (hemoglobin 11.7 g/dL, MCV 78.0 fL), hypoalbuminemia (3.3 g/dL), proteinuria (552 mg/dL)
History of bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome with surgical release 2 years prior to symptom onset, suggesting earlier amyloid deposition in peripheral nerves
Treatment initiated with bortezomib, lenalidomide, dexamethasone for myeloma and doxycycline for cardiac amyloidosis with supportive heart failure management

One year after treatment initiation: completed induction therapy, consolidation with autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, on bortezomib maintenance therapy with complete resolution of heart failure symptoms and return to normal functional status

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Oral thrush or mechanical tongue biting
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Initial otolaryngology evaluation attributed indentations to tongue biting and treated for oral thrush, but persistent symptoms despite treatment and subsequent biopsy revealed AL amyloid, not thrush or mechanical injury

Multisystem involvement (tongue, periorbital plaques, peripheral nerves, heart) with confirmed AL amyloid on biopsy and monoclonal lambda light chain with underlying plasma cell myeloma indicates systemic AL amyloidosis, not isolated cardiomyopathy

Otolaryngology re-evaluation specifically noted absence of overt macroglossia despite persistent tongue symptoms, and biopsy confirmed amyloid deposition rather than other causes of tongue enlargement

remaining_uncertainties: Specific timing of when the patient first developed the bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome relative to other systemic symptoms (documented as 2 years prior to tongue symptom onset, but exact onset date not specified)
Whether cardiac MRI was performed to further characterize the infiltrative pattern and confirm amyloid deposition in the myocardium
Long-term follow-up data beyond 1 year post-treatment initiation regarding sustained remission, light chain normalization, and cardiac function recovery
